messages.author: 2f71cb707147be6f
messages.subject: Overide bootstrap placement of blocks
parts:
This may be obvious to you html/css experts, but I can't figure out how to place three uiOutput blocks next to each other horizontally instead of the vertical placement that happens naturally. I've tried several things that work on simple bits, but I can't get it to work with the shiny/bootstrap stuff.
Here's an example that creates the three blocks and my latest unsuccessful attempt to place them horizontally:

ui.R
library(shiny)

shinyUI(basicPage(

  numericInput("n", "N", 4),
  br(),

div(
  style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: text-top; ",
  div(class="btn-group btn-group-vertical",
    uiOutput("Bbuttons")
  ),
  div(uiOutput("alpha")),
  div(class="btn-group btn-group-vertical",
    uiOutput("Fbuttons")
  )
),

  br()
))

server.R
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {

  output$Fbuttons <- renderUI({
    lapply(1:input$n, function(i) { actionButton(paste0("btnF",i), "+") })
  })

  output$Bbuttons <- renderUI({
    lapply(1:input$n, function(i) { actionButton(paste0("btnB",i), "-") })
  })

  output$alpha <- renderTable({
    data.frame(Data=1:input$n, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  })


})

I really want the buttons lined up with the lines of the table so the user can alter a row at a time by pressing the appropriate button.
I can fiddle with heights later to make it nicer.
A perfect solution would be essentially a data.frame with buttons in the first and last columns.
(I need a solution that doesn't use shiny incubator, which I cannot use for various reasons.)
I left out the server code that responds to the button clicks since it is irrelevant for this topic.

Thanks,
David Reiner

messages.subject: Re: Overide bootstrap placement of blocks
parts:
Hi,

You might use
tags$div(class="span4", firstButton),
tags$div(class="span4", secondButton),
tags$div(class="span4", thirdButton)

For styling issues, the best is to refer to bootstrap documentation.

HTH,

Robin

    <div class="list">
    <table class="tbl" border="1">
      <tbody><tr>
        <td><button id="btnF1" type="button" class="btn action-button">+</button></td>

        <td>__B1__</td>
        <td><button id="btnB1" type="button" class="btn action-button">-</button></td>

        <td><button id="btnF2" type="button" class="btn action-button">+</button></td>

        <td><button id="btnB2" type="button" class="btn action-button">-</button></td>

')

Does anyone have a clever way of accomplishing this with my original columns of buttons and table?

David
